_comment: EXAMPLE · MongoDB destination / write modes — the destination that does not fit the `tables` + `if_table_exists` mould. It writes DOCUMENTS, so it takes collections_with_ids (a list of (collection, id_field) PAIRS, one write slot each; id_field=None lets MongoDB generate _id) and if_collection_exists ("append", or "replace" which DROPS the collection — indexes and all, not a truncate). Four sinks: write_append (explicit id, so a re-run collides under the default update_existing=False), write_replace (generated ids), write_upsert (update_existing=True turns each write into an upsert on the id field — the only idempotent, merge-like sink in these examples, which no SQL or warehouse destination here can do), write_two_collections (note the id fields differ per entry, which is why the pair carries it). BSON converts Date/Time/Duration on the way in; Decimal round-trips exactly. One function per file under functions/mongodb_dest_modes/. Run: `tdx-xp oneshot --suite examples/mongodb_dest_modes --keep`.
